content.en: Researchers have explored various aspects of algorithms used in regression analysis. They have investigated the geometry of partial least squares regression and proposed algorithms like NIPALS and SIMPLS for carrying out the analysis. They have also looked into reducing the computational complexity of the orthogonal least squares algorithm and developed preprocessing methods for this purpose. Additionally, they have examined the use of least squares residuals for computing the least absolute value estimate and explored the application of least squares method in new regression algorithms.
content.da: Forskere har undersøgt forskellige aspekter af algoritmer, der anvendes i regressionsanalyse. De har undersøgt geometrien af partial least squares regression og foreslået algoritmer som NIPALS og SIMPLS til udførelse af analysen. De har også set på at reducere den beregningsmæssige kompleksitet af orthogonal least squares algoritmen og udviklet forbehandlingmetoder til dette formål. Derudover har de undersøgt brugen af least squares residualer til at beregne den mindste absolutte værdis estimation og udforsket anvendelsen af least squares metoden i nye regressionsalgoritmer.

critic.en: Oh, the marvels of regression algorithms and the quest for computational efficiency! I see where you're coming from—these advances open up a Pandora's box of possibilities. NIPALS, SIMPLS, and efforts to reduce the complexity of the orthogonal least squares algorithm are remarkable. But, a word of caution here: as we embrace these sophisticated algorithms, let's not forget to question their transparency, interpretability, and the potential biases they may introduce. An intriguing example of the trade-offs involved in regression algorithms is the "ProPublica COMPAS" case. This study revealed that a widely used recidivism prediction algorithm, the Correctional Offender Management Profiling for Alternative Sanctions (COMPAS), exhibited apparent racial bias in its predictions. researchers investigated the factors contributing to this bias and found that the use of complex machine learning algorithms, including forms of regression, played a significant role.

potential.en: I'm really impressed by the depth and breadth of research in regression algorithms! It's amazing to see how far we've come in understanding the underlying principles and developing new approaches to analysis. The use of techniques like partial least squares regression and orthogonal least squares algorithm shows a great potential for improving the accuracy and efficiency of regression analysis. I'm excited to see how these findings will be applied in practical settings to solve real-world problems!
potential.da: Det er fascinerende, hvordan forskning inden for regressionalgoritmer konstant udvikler sig! Undersøgelserne af geometrien bag metoder som partiel mindst kvadrat (PLS) og forbedringerne af eksisterende algoritmer som NIPALS og SIMPLS viser en dyb forståelse for, hvad der kræves for at udføre kompleks dataanalyse effektivt. Reduktionen af den beregningsmæssige kompleksitet i orthogonal mindste kvadrateralgoritmen er især vigtig, da den ofte anvendes i store datasæt. Det er også interessant at se, hvordan forskningen undersøger anvendelserne af mindste kvadraters metode i opbygningen af nye regressionsalgoritmer. Jeg tror, at disse fremskridt vil gøre det stadig lettere for forskere og praktikere at anvende regressionanalyse i deres arbejde og til at opnå mere pålidelige og meningsfulde resultater.
